newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish fund breaks deal with management firm.
newsitem.headline: Polish fund breaks deal with management firm.

text.p: The supervisory board of Poland's National Investment Fund (NFI) No. 2 has withdrawn from an agreement on Thursday with a firm managing the fund, Hevelius Management sp. z o.o., PAP news agency reported.
PAP gave no further details and fund's officials were not immediately available for comment.
NFI No. 2 is one of 15 such institutions created under Poland's mass privatisation programme.
The funds, controlling some 500 mid-size companies, have hired consortia of foreign and domestic companies to manage the fund's portfolio, restructure the companies and find investors for them.
The consortium managing NFI No. 2 included NP International Holding with a 50-percent stake, Bank Gdanski, which holds a 40-percent equity, and Murray Johnstone Poland Ltd.
In November, Bank Gdanski SA said it planned to sell its stake in Hevelius, saying the move is necessary to protect its interests.
